source.title: Rethinking generalization of classifiers in separable classes scenarios and over-parameterized regimes
source.authors: Julius Martinetz; C. Linse; T. Martinetz

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports training classification outcomes for over-parameterized neural networks on CIFAR-10 and MNIST, but uses LAMB rather than the SGD or Adam named in V1.
record.gate_note: The separable-class experiments use a perceptron, and the paper assumes ERM reaches a global minimum; neither is evidence about gradient-based neural-network training. The neural-network experiments explicitly report zero training error after training.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own zero training classification error results for randomly initialized convolutional networks, including on CIFAR-10. LAMB provides a different optimization method from V1's SGD or Adam; MNIST provides an additional setting.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the empirical zero-error outcome but understates the central conclusion. The authors argue that bad-generalizing global minima become rarer as training sample size increases, and develop a density-of-classifiers model whose learning curves approximately fit MNIST and CIFAR-10 results. Larger ResNets need fewer samples to approach their fitted minimum generalization error; the MLPs do not show that trend.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains randomly initialized neural networks to zero training error on benchmark image datasets, but uses LAMB rather than SGD or Adam; its reported neural-network experiments assess generalization as well as training error.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, architecture, and number of training samples vary across the experiments; the paper reports zero training error throughout these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: MLP3 and MLP8 also achieve zero training classification error on clean CIFAR-10 using LAMB.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large fully connected ReLU networks trained with LAMB can interpolate clean CIFAR-10 training sets.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN), 2024
record.problems: The neural-network training-error report does not give a separate uncertainty estimate for that measure. The paper reports zero training error but does not test CIFAR-100, corrupted labels, or SGD/Adam.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible reported neural-network training-error results left out. The separable-class perceptron experiments are excluded because they do not test the claim's gradient-trained neural networks.

untested.parts: SGD or Adam; CIFAR-100; corrupted or random labels; smaller convolutional models; early stopping; regularized recipes. No training-time or optimization-failure distribution is reported.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious optimization minima, and extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth and comparisons between plain networks and identity-shortcut networks.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, training speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, catapult recovery, and divergence.
Training speed or learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The theoretical analysis assumes successful ERM and is not an optimization convergence proof. Its bad minima concern generalization among zero-training-error solutions, not V2's spurious local minima. Learning speed in the fitted curves means sample efficiency, not optimization speed. Random-label outcomes are cited from prior work, not measured here.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, SGD or Adam, smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes. It uses LAMB.
